title: Active Data lets a named Responsible Party edit records inside the Artifact without going through the Root Edit process
content:
Alongside the `[Core]` documents that make up the Artifact, several documents are tagged `[Active Data Controller]` and `[Active Data]`. A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.1.3.4 is typical: "The Distribution Reward payments ... are defined as Active Data. The Active Data is updated as follows: The Responsible Party is Operational GovOps. The Update Process must follow the protocol for 'Direct Edit'."

This is the release valve for a governance system whose normal amendment path takes a 1% proposer, a seven-day Facilitator review and a three-day poll. Payment records change every reward period; routing them through Root Edit would be absurd. Active Data carves out a class of content that lives *inside* the Artifact but is maintained operationally.

The carve-out is bounded in three ways rather than being a general exception. It is **declared per document**, so what is directly editable is enumerated in advance, not decided at edit time. It **names a Responsible Party** — Operational GovOps, not Skybase itself — so the entity writing payment records is the same one that reviews the Agent's rebate calculations, and is not the Agent. And it **names a protocol**, 'Direct Edit', so the update path is itself a specified process.

The design principle is a clean split between rules and records: `[Core]` documents state what must happen and change only by governance; `[Active Data]` documents state what did happen and change by operation. The risk is boundary creep — anything reclassified as Active Data effectively exits token holder control, so the classification decision is where scrutiny belongs.
description: Reward payment lists and partner payment addresses are declared Active Data with Operational GovOps as Responsible Party and 'Direct Edit' as the update protocol.
